title: Validating a pydantic-settings BaseSettings reads the environment
question: Under pydantic-settings 2.16.1, does validating a BaseSettings subclass from stored data (model_validate({}), model_validate({"b": 2}), model_validate_json("{}")) read the current environment, so that a stored run option or method params re-read through such a class would silently mix in the environment?
method: A BaseSettings subclass with env_prefix P0Q_SETTINGS_ENV_ and two int fields (a, b, default 0) and a plain BaseModel of the same shape, validated three ways with P0Q_SETTINGS_ENV_A=1 set in the process environment; each result is compared with a hand-written expectation (BaseSettings a=1 from the environment, BaseModel a=0; a stored b=2 kept by both). Probe environment build/probe-venv (Python 3.14.10, pydantic 2.14.1, pydantic-settings 2.16.1).

agents.separation: coordinator brief; wrote only code/settings_env.py, results/settings-env/, records/p0q.settings-env.json and a README section

results.name: calls_reading_environment
results.note: model_validate({}), model_validate({"b": 2}) and model_validate_json("{}") on the BaseSettings all returned a=1 from P0Q_SETTINGS_ENV_A

results.name: base_model_reading_environment
results.note: the plain BaseModel kept the default a=0 in every call

conclusion: Under pydantic-settings 2.16.1 every validation entry point of a BaseSettings (model_validate with an empty or partial dict, model_validate_json) runs the settings sources and fills unset fields from the environment, while explicitly supplied values are kept; a plain BaseModel does not. Re-reading a stored payload through a BaseSettings therefore mixes in the current environment, which supports coordinator decision 26: only Settings is a BaseSettings, and operations models, run options and method params stay frozen BaseModels.
